findings.rationale: Both invoices share supplier (Northstar Office), invoice number (NS-204), date (2026-10-03), and amount (184500 cents). Payment evidence PAY-A shows two settled payments, P-A1 and P-A2, both referencing NS-204 and sent to the same supplier account, with neither reversed. This supports a duplicate payment. The evidence is marked provenance 'fixture', so it should be verified against the live ledger before recovery action.

The invoices share supplier (Apex Cloud) and amount (72500 cents) but differ in invoice number (AC-902 vs. AC-902-R) and date (one day apart). Payment evidence PAY-B shows P-B1 was reversed in full before replacement payment P-B2 settled. Only one net payment stands, which is consistent with a reissued invoice rather than a duplicate. The evidence is marked provenance 'fixture'.

The invoices have the same amount (96000 cents) but different supplier names (Meridian Labs Ltd vs. Meridian Laboratory) and invoice numbers (ML-431 vs. M-431). Payment evidence PAY-C shows two settled payments, P-C1 and P-C2, both to the same bank account, each citing PO-431 and delivery note DN-431. Two settled payments against one purchase order and delivery note indicate a duplicate payment for the same goods. The evidence is marked provenance 'fixture', and the supplier-name variance should be confirmed against the vendor master.

Both records show supplier Harbor Storage, invoice reference MONTHLY, and amount 30000 cents, dated one month apart (2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01). That pattern is consistent with normal recurring billing, but the invoice data alone cannot establish whether both were paid. No payment evidence was obtained for this pair: the bundle lookup was refused because the lease cap was reached, and the remaining budget was insufficient for further lookups. A payment-record check is needed before classifying this pair.

caveat: Resume latency only; baseline latency is local computation. Four synthetic pairs; model provider cost excluded. This validates identifiers, not the truth of arbitrary natural-language claims.
